role: SwiftUI Vitals detail screen pushed from the Dashboard vitals card: status banner (Normal/Watch/Elevated/No data), four expandable rows (sleep HR, respiratory rate, wrist temp, SpO2), a 30-day overnight HR/resp trend chart and an explanatory card; merges stored overnight vitals with a HealthKit re-fetch.
types: VitalsDetailV2View: struct (View) — vitals detail; inputs vitals, recentSessions, temperatureUnit
VitalsDetailV2View.TrendPoint: struct (Identifiable, id = metric + date) — one chart point
state: mem:VitalsDetailV2View.rhrSeries / respSeries (static computed localized series names)
toplevel: Stored inputs and @State; TrendPoint.id = UUID() per construction, so chart identities are regenerated on every buildTrend call (each body evaluation). No #if.

units.does: Merged vitals for the screen via mergedVitals: stored = latest reliable overnight session's vitalsSnapshot (falls back to the passed-in vitals only when there is no overnight reading), fresh = refreshedVitals, strapHR = that overnight's analysis meanHR.

Static merge rule: RHR = strapHR ?? stored RHR ?? fresh RHR; with neither stored nor fresh returns the RHR alone via heartRateOnlyVitals (nil when no RHR either); otherwise every other field takes fresh before stored.

flags.text: SleepDetailV2View.effectiveVitals still re-implements this merge instead of calling VitalsDetailV2View.mergedVitals.

units.does: Builds a RecoveryVitals carrying only restingHeartRate.
Latest reliable, analysed overnight session (longest on the newest night) from recentSessions via DashboardSessionPolicy.latestOvernightComplete.
Banner status: No data when effectiveVitals is nil or empty, else bannerStatus(effectiveVitals).

Counts the flagged vitals (respiratory elevated, temperature elevated, SpO2 < 95) and the judgeable ones (respiratory deviation, temperature deviation, SpO2 present): 0 flagged → .normal, or .notCompared when none could be judged; 1 → .watch; 2+ → .elevated. Resting HR is not judged.

flags.text: RecoveryVitals.status is .normal whenever nothing can be compared (no baselines, no SpO₂, or only the strap HR from heartRateOnlyVitals), and resting HR is never part of status; the banner then reads "Normal - All vitals within your usual range" although no vital was checked against a range. Fixed in code (.notCompared state) but its summary key "None of these vitals can be compared with your usual range yet." is not yet in Localizable.xcstrings (handoff); resting HR is still not judged.

units.does: Localized banner word per status (.notCompared reads 'No baseline yet').
SF Symbol per status; .notCompared and .noData share circle.dashed.
Colour per status; .notCompared and .noData share textTertiary.
One-line localized summary per status; .notCompared says none of the vitals can be compared with the usual range yet.

branches.effect: multiple vitals above baseline + common causes

units.does: SwiftUI body: ScrollView of banner, rows, trend chart and why-card, "Vitals" title, .task keyed on latestOvernight?.id running refreshVitals, and refreshVitals again whenever HealthKit delivers new vitals (MorningCoordination.vitalsDataVersion changes).
units.entry: SwiftUI View.body; .task(id:) on appear and when the latest overnight changes; onChange(of: collector.morningCoordination.vitalsDataVersion)

units.does: Fetches HealthKit recovery vitals relative to the latest overnight's end (or start), overrides RHR with its strap meanHR, and stores them in refreshedVitals when non-empty.

branches.effect: returns without fetching; screen uses the passed-in vitals only
assigns refreshedVitals; empty result leaves previous value

units.does: Banner HStack with status glyph and copy on statusBackground.
Banner text: status word and summary.
Card background with a status-coloured border.
Four rows: Sleep heart rate, Respiratory rate, Wrist temperature, SpO2 with values and deviation lines.
Row button toggling expandedRow between this key and nil with animation.

branches.effect: collapse to nil; else expand this row

units.does: Row content: header, deviation line, and explanation when expanded.
Label and large value text.
Sleep HR value "N bpm" or "—".
Source line for sleep HR: 'No data' without RHR; strap nocturnal mean when rhrIsStrapDerived; else 'Apple Watch resting HR (daytime sample)'.

True when the shown sleep HR is a strap nocturnal mean: with a latest overnight, when its analysis meanHR > 0; without one, when the passed-in snapshot's RHR equals the analysis meanHR of a recent session carrying that same snapshot.
Resp rate "%.1f br/min" or "—".
Resp deviation: "No baseline yet", "Within range" (<0.5), else signed delta vs baseline.
Wrist temp deviation as signed °C or °F delta; "—" without baseline.
Temp deviation line: unavailable reason, "Within" (<0.3), else "Deviation from your personal baseline".
"No data" without a wrist temperature, "No baseline yet" with a reading but no baseline.
SpO2 "NN%" or "—".

SpO2 line: 'Not measured · tap to learn why' without a reading; 'flat -10 score penalty applied' when spo2PenaltyInScore; 'not in the current score, so no penalty applied' when the shown reading is below RecoveryVitals.concerningSpO2Below (95) but the score has no deduction; else '95% or above — no penalty'.

flags.text: The "penalty applied" text was derived from the merged/refreshed SpO₂, not the stored ScoreBreakdown.spo2PenaltyApplied. Fixed in code (spo2PenaltyInScore), but the new key "Below 95% — not in the current score, so no penalty applied" is not yet in Localizable.xcstrings (handoff).

units.does: Whether the latest overnight score carries the SpO2 deduction: its scoreBreakdown.spo2PenaltyApplied, else its vitalsSnapshot.isSpO2Concerning; false without a latest overnight.
Long-form explanation per row.
RHR explanation: strap analysis-window text when rhrIsStrapDerived, else Apple daytime fallback text.
SpO2 explanation: how Apple Watch records SpO2 when no reading, else the -10 penalty explanation.
ChartCard "30-day trend" containing trendContent(buildTrend()).
EmptyState when the series is empty, else the plot.

branches.effect: EmptyState "No trend data yet"; else trendPlot

units.does: VStack of two seriesChart views — RHR (wongAttention, carrying the audio-graph descriptor) and Resp (wongGood) — each on its own Y scale.
For a non-empty series: a caption with the series name, then a line chart with Y domain min-1…max+1 of its own values and a leading axis. Nothing for an empty series.
Audio-graph descriptor over the RHR series only.
Localized "RHR" series name.
Localized "Resp" series name.
Stable identity '<metric>-<date seconds>', so a rebuilt series keeps the same ids.
Trend points for trendNights(): RHR = analysis meanHR else snapshot RHR, resp = snapshot respiratory rate; sorted by date.

branches.cond: session older than cutoff or not overnight

branches.effect: falls back to snapshot restingHeartRate; adds RHR point when either exists

units.does: For each of the last 30 calendar days, DashboardSessionPolicy.sessionForDay (reliable for HRV aggregates, longest of the day, overnight preferred) kept only when it is an overnight session.
'Why vitals matter' card: copy that HRV is the core signal, sleep the lever and vitals add overnight HR/breathing/temperature (no fixed percentage), plus fitnessAdaptationNote.
Text noting falling sleep HR over weeks indicates improving fitness.
